extracted.intended_audience: journalists, editorial writers, and those hiring or training newspaper staff
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and implicit standards for running an editorial page: qualities sought in editorial writing, how to judge and select writers and secretaries, and practical criteria for evaluating descriptions, residences, and staff potential. Drawn from Joseph Pulitzer's practices and tastes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Describing people (precision of physical description)
rubrics_metrics.description: Everything had to be given in feet and inches and in definite colors. You had to exercise your utmost powers to describe the exact cast of the features, the peculiar texture and growth of the hair, the expression of the eyes, and every little trick of gait or gesture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not accept vague, average descriptions. Provide precise measurements, specific colors, exact feature-casts, hair texture/growth, expressions, and distinctive gestures or gait. Re-test descriptions later to reveal observers' inability to agree; accuracy should survive re-description.

rubrics_metrics.name: Editorial writing — three cardinal qualities
rubrics_metrics.description: J. P.'s theory of editorial writing ... called for three cardinal qualities--brevity, directness and style
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Editorials should be concise, to the point, and stylistically effective. Because these qualities are hard to achieve under pressure, limit writers' output (Pulitzer tried to limit each man to an average of half a column a day) so they can craft pieces with these qualities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Close metrics of editorial style
rubrics_metrics.description: He watched the style of each man with the closest attention, examining the length of the paragraphs, of the sentences, of the words, the variety of the vocabulary, the choice of adjectives and adverbs, the employment of superlatives, the selection of a heading, the nicety of adjustment between the thought to be expressed and the language employed for its expression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess editorial style quantitatively and qualitatively: paragraph/sentence/word length, vocabulary variety, adjective/adverb use, restraint in superlatives, appropriateness of headline, and precision of diction matching the thought. Send exemplary phrases to staff as teaching models.

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection of new writers (sample-work and biography requirement)
rubrics_metrics.description: If he read an editorial which impressed him ... he put it on one side ... make a representative collection of the unknown man's writings ... find out who the author was and request that he would supply what he considered to be a fair sample of his work, a dozen or more articles, and a brief biography of himself.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Vet prospective writers by assembling representative clippings across time, then request a substantial sample (a dozen+ pieces) plus a brief bio. Subject candidates to extended, exacting review (the 'gauntlet of his judgment') before hiring.

rubrics_metrics.name: Condensation and efficient selection of reading material
rubrics_metrics.description: Lists of the titles of all the articles and abstracts of all the more important ones ... I had fifteen ready ... 'I'll allow you four minutes for each of them.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prepare condensed abstracts and prioritized lists of articles for rapid consumption and selection. Use strict time limits to surface what truly merits full attention and to maintain editorial pace.

rubrics_metrics.name: System of searching examination for staff evaluation
rubrics_metrics.description: He developed a system of searching examination before which no subterfuge could stand. ... J. P.'s questions covered names, places, dates, motives, the chain of causation, what you said, what you did, what you felt, what you thought ... worked backward and forward until all that you had ever thought or done ... had been disclosed to him so far as he was interested to know it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate potential or current staff by probing memory, motives, chronology, decisions, feelings, and reasoning; cross-check over time and in multiple directions. Use persistent, comprehensive questioning and document responses (written statements) to reveal competence, candor, and reliability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attitude toward testimonials/references
rubrics_metrics.description: He complained that scores of men had come to him with references ... references of such a character that their happy possessors might ... have applied for the Chief Justiceship ... 'No, no; if a man brings references it proves nothing; but if he can't, it proves a great deal.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat glowing testimonials skeptically—presence of references is weak evidence of ability. Pay attention when candidates cannot produce references, as that absence is more informative and potentially disqualifying.

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation by potential and trainability (development over record)
rubrics_metrics.description: What you knew and what you were able to do, once you had reached a certain standard, became secondary in his interest to what you could be made to know and what you could be taught to do. Growth and development were the chief aims of his discipline.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess employees not merely by past accomplishments but by potential for learning and development; assign tasks to broaden capabilities; prefer those who show teachability and capacity to grow.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for selecting residences (villa-seeker standard)
rubrics_metrics.description: The villa-seeker ... to gather a mass of information about its climate, its amenities, its resident and floating population, its accessibility by sea and land, the opportunities for hearing good music, and to report in the minutest detail upon all available houses ... maps, plans, and photographs ... Particular attention was paid to the streets and to the country roads in the neighborhood, as it was necessary to have facilities for motoring, for riding, and for walking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When choosing residences for a principal, compile comprehensive local intelligence: climate, amenities, demographics, transport access, cultural opportunities, maps/plans/photos, and road conditions; specify needed alterations (e.g., door silencers, double windows) to ensure quiet and habitability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Literary qualities admired (taste metrics)
rubrics_metrics.description: He found in [Macaulay's writings] most of the qualities which he admired--great descriptive power, political acumen, satire, neatness of phrase, apt comparisons and analogies, and shrewd analysis of character.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Value prose that combines descriptive power, political insight, incisive satire, concise phrasing, apt analogy, and strong character analysis. Use exemplars (favorite paragraphs) as instructive models for staff.

rubrics_metrics.name: Attention to the 'sound' and exact equivalence in translation and phrasing
rubrics_metrics.description: He was never tired of discussing literary style, ... the different SOUND of the same idea expressed in different languages ... compare lines ... Of the former pair he greatly preferred the English, of the latter the German. Sometimes we discussed at great length the exact English equivalent of some German or French word.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider not only semantic equivalence but the phonetic and stylistic 'sound' of phrasing; prefer translations and word choices that preserve both meaning and the appropriate aural/style impact.
